jobs.occupation: EY-Parthenon - Senior Consultant - Technology in M&A
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 1706128

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

As you write your next chapter, what shape will it take?

Are you ready to take the next step in your M&A career and work on some of the most exciting deals in the market? We are looking for a Senior Consultant to join our Transaction Strategy and Execution team in Copenhagen.

In this role, you will be part of a high-performing team that supports clients across the full deal lifecycle: from M&A strategy to execution. You will work closely with clients on complex, high-impact engagements, where your insights and capabilities will drive real results. At the same time, you will play an active role in shaping our team, contributing to a strong culture and supporting the development of future leaders.

Shape your future with confidence.

Skills and attributes for success

You are analytically strong and comfortable working with complex data and problem-solving, using AI-enabled tools to enhance analysis and insight generation. You bring a structured and pragmatic approach, combined with strong business understanding and attention to detail.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and can manage ambiguity while maintaining focus on delivering high-quality outcomes. At the same time, you communicate clearly and confidently, translating complexity into actionable insights for both clients and colleagues.

You bring experience from client-facing or in-house roles across M&A execution (pre- and/or post-deal) and operational delivery, for example:

• Product and technology diligence

• Assessment of the product portfolio and roadmap, together with the underlying technology and R&D setup to evaluate commercial attractiveness/value creation potential

• IT diligence

• Evaluating the IT environments, from strategy to costs, to identify risks and opportunities, and to inform the investment case

• Technology integration and separation

• Leading technology workstreams, from strategy to execution/operationalization

• Digital value creation

• Assessing digital and AI-driven value creation opportunities, and implications for the deal theses and post-deal value capture

As a Senior Consultant, you will work across a range of M&A engagements spanning M&A strategy, operational diligence, as well as value creation and deal management. You are passionate about the operational aspects of M&A, thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments, and build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Conducting operational due diligence/value creation analysis

• Managing and driving workstreams across pre- and post-deal engagements

• Supporting business development through pitch content, proposals and client conversations

What we look for

As our new colleague you bring 3-6 years of experience from strategy and M&A consulting or industry experience. You bring an inclusive approach, building strong relationships with both clients and colleagues and are a strong communicator who can translate complex ideas into clear and actionable insights. You take ownership of your work with a consistent focus on quality and impact.

What’s in it for you

• Work on complex, high-profile M&A and divestment engagements

• Collaborate with integrated teams across geographies and disciplines

• Continuous coaching, feedback and formal learning to support your development

• A purpose-led culture focused on creating long-term value for clients and society

• Hybrid work model, balancing in-office and client-site collaboration with flexibility

• A role with broad responsibility and room to shape how we deliver and grow

What you can expect during the recruitment process

• Interview process will include a take-home case and an on-the-spot case

• Your CV gives us the basics; a strong cover letter helps us understand your motivation and relevant experience beyond M&A consulting

Please submit your application no later than 1 December 2026. Selection and interviews are ongoing. If you have any questions or need more information about the role, please contact Malthe Pedersen at malthe.t.pedersen@parthenon.ey.com. For questions regarding the recruitment process, contact Jakob Damsted at jakob.damsted@dk.ey.com.

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

Highlights:

• Full-Stack Python/TS engineer needed for a B2B SaaS startup in Copenhagen (with plenty of traction!)

• We have a lean, get-stuff-done team. No annoying extra management layers or unnecessary bureaucratic rituals. And we are "AI-forward" in our own development practices.

• You will own features end to end, from the data model through to the screen, on a platform that manufacturers rely on to keep production lines running.

• You will work in a small engineering team, directly with the person who decides what we build, and the problems you spend your time on are hard because the domain is hard, not because the organization is.

• We're building legitimately useful tools for the industries and companies that make the world go around.... manufacturers. Both AI-tools and just "plain-old-good-software" tools.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality, all in a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth.

The platform now covers more ground than the team that built it. We are hiring engineers to keep that pace sustainable, and to go deeper on the parts of the product our customers are pushing hardest.

The role

You will join a small engineering team and work across the whole stack: Python on the backend, TypeScript on the frontend and in the AI layers. There is no split between people who design and people who implement. You will take a problem from a customer conversation or a product decision through to something running in production for real manufacturers.

You will work directly with our co-founder and CEO, who is a hands-on product builder himself. That means short conversations instead of tickets thrown over a wall, and it means your questions about why something should work a certain way get answered by the person who decided it.

The domain is genuinely complicated, and that is the interesting part. Supplier relationships in automotive involve deep hierarchies, long-running approval processes, strict audit requirements and a lot of state that has to be exactly right. Modeling that well is most of the job.

Title and level flex with experience. We are open to strong mid-level engineers and to senior engineers who want more scope than their current company gives them.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and on a codebase with this much implicit context, working through problems with the rest of the team in person is much faster than doing it in writing. Sensible flexibility when you need it is a given; full-time remote is not what we are offering.

Our current stack:

• Backend: Python / Django

• Frontend: Vue (but no specific Vue experience is needed)

• Infrastructure: AWS (mostly)

• Agents: Cloudflare (TypeScript) + Claude & OpenAI platform

What you will do

• Build features end to end, from data model and backend logic through to the TypeScript frontend our customers actually click on.

• Build end-to-end / front-to-back AI features (in-app AI assistants, background worker agents, email-routing agents, customer-configurable agent framework components)

• Design and evolve the relational data model that sits under supplier relationships, approvals and quality records.

• Take vaguely defined customer problems and turn them into something specific enough to build, then build it.

• Work on integrations between Supplios and customer systems (ERP and adjacent tooling), where failures have visible consequences for a production line.

• Improve the parts of the codebase that need it, rather than routing around them.

• Review other people's code and have yours reviewed; we keep the loop tight and unbureaucratic.

• Help keep the platform healthy in production across our regions: errors, performance and the boring things that keep customers trusting us.

• Take part in product decisions. Engineers here are expected to have opinions about what we build, not just how.

What we are looking for

Essential

• Professional experience with Python. This is not negotiable; the backend is Python and you need to be effective in it.

• Solid TypeScript experience and genuine comfort working on the frontend.

• Experience building and running SaaS products, including the part after launch where real users depend on them.

• AI-forward development techniques. (This does not mean you no longer write code.)

• A track record of owning work end to end without waiting to be told what to do next.

• The temperament for a small, senior company: high ownership, low ceremony.

• You want to work primarily from an office in central Copenhagen, with a small team.

Nice to have

Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. Nobody has all of these.

• Experience with B2B enterprise SaaS, especially where customers are large and demanding and implementations are not self-serve. This is a significant plus.

• Experience with complex relational data modeling, and with large, long-lived codebases that you did not write yourself. A big plus.

• Experience building AI-based products, using the latest frameworks/harnesses and infrastructure components (including RAG) is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with any of: domain-driven design, the actor model, finite state machines, CQRS, event-driven architecture. We use these ideas where they earn their place, and it helps if the vocabulary is already yours.

• Startup experience, particularly early stage. A significant plus.

• Knowledge of manufacturing, automotive or supply chain. Useful, but we can teach you the domain; we cannot teach you the craft, so do not rule yourself out on this.

Language

English is the only important language for this position; we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• The scope is unusually large for the stage. You are one of a small number of engineers on a platform that serves demanding customers globally. What you build ships, and it ships soon.

• No layers between you and the decisions. You work directly with the co-founder and CEO, who runs product. There is no committee to navigate and nobody to translate your work for you.

• Hard problems that are not artificially hard. The complexity comes from the domain (hierarchies, state, audit trails, integrations that must not fail), not from organisational overhead.

• Real customers already, and real gaps. The product has paying customers in automotive and clear places where it needs to get better. Both halves of that are true, and both are why this is a good job.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

Our common goal is to implement outstanding and innovative projects worldwide.

Click here and sign up for our applicant training:
For Danish applicants: https://hrcaseforum.simplero.com/page/240347-beumer-ansoeger

For English applicants: https://hrcaseforum.simplero.com/page/243727-beumer-applicant

WHAT BENEFITS DO WE OFFER?

• 
We offer exciting opportunities in an internationally operating family-owned company with locations in more than 70 countries – including the opportunity to temporarily work from one of our international locations as part of our Flex Abroad Program.

• 
During our immersive onboarding program in, you will receive an extensive overview of BEUMER Group, our history, and our vision for the future, whilst also getting to know your new colleagues.

Through a culture of open feedback, transparent corporate updates, and regular employee events, we actively cultivate a friendly, open, and collaborative working environment

Your personal and professional growth is integral to our ethos. We champion your development through a wide range of training courses and upskilling opportunities — including support for external courses and grants for trainees.

Flexible working hours and the choice of operating from a remote office are important components of our modern work culture, much like our bright, spacious offices and ergonomically optimized workstations.

Your health matters to us. Enjoy free access to our on-site fitness centre and join one of our many sports clubs for a healthier, more connected work-life. We also provide computer glasses subsidies, vegetarian lunch options, and free fresh fruit to help boost your well-being.

From accident insurance to attractive company pension schemes and health insurance for you and your children, we are committed to supporting your long-term well-being.

Supporting you when you are not in work is also important to us. Our Staff Association organizes and sponsors social, cultural, and sporting activities, including our annual Christmas and Summer parties, which are always great fun.

• 
Sustainability is one of our key core values, which we tackle on multiple fronts. For example, you will have access to our electric charging stations in the employee parking area, with the electricity being provided at cost price.

Fair pay is extended to all our employees, and we ensure we provide a balanced and equitable remuneration framework. You will also receive a number of additional salary benefits that combine to form an attractive salary package.

• 
Everyone needs a rest and a break from work at some point. That is why you will receive 30 days of vacation days per year, as well as various other special holiday days. We also provide extra support for maternity and paternity leave.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

jobs.occupation: Kok søges til Ristorante Sole d'Italia i hjertet af København / Chef Wanted
jobs.description:
Ristorante Sole d'Italia ligger på Gråbrødretorv midt i København. Vi laver klassisk italiensk mad fra bunden – håndlavet brød, frisk pasta og sæsonens råvarer. Vi søger nu en kok til vores køkken.

Om jobbet

Du laver italiensk mad fra bunden sammen med resten af køkkenet: forretter, pasta og hovedretter. Du er med til forberedelsen om formiddagen og kører din station under service.

Vi forventer

Erfaring fra et professionelt køkken. At du kan holde tempoet og overblikket en travl aften. At du arbejder rent og struktureret. Dansk eller engelsk i det daglige.

Vi tilbyder

We're looking for a Performance Tooling Engineer to own the tooling and automated tests that keep our products fast, efficient, and correct. Your mission is to catch regressions before they ship, across latency, memory, power/thermals and functionality, by building the test harnesses, benchmarks, and CI infrastructure that make regressions visible, reproducible, and actionable. Design, write, and maintain automated tests that detect performance regressions (latency, memory footprint, power consumption, etc.) and functional regressions.

• 
Build and operate CI pipelines and tooling that run these tests reliably across a fleet of hardware devices.

• 
Create dashboards, alerting, and triage tooling that surface regressions early and help engineers root-cause them quickly, e.g. automated bisection, historical trend tracking.

• 
Partner with cross-functional teams & leadership to define meaningful performance goals and acceptance criteria.

• 
Continuously improve test coverage, execution speed, flakiness, and the developer experience of running and interpreting tests.

• 
Very strong problem-solving and coding skills.

• 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• 
Experience building and maintaining CI systems.

• 
Solid understanding of performance measurement fundamentals: how to benchmark reliably, control for noise, and reason about latency, memory, and power/thermal metrics.

• 
Experience writing automated tests and the tooling/frameworks around them.

• 
Proven track record of integrating AI tools to enhance both personal productivity and team workflows.

• 
Experience developing for Apple platforms (iOS/macOS), with working knowledge of Swift.

• 
Familiarity with the Apple development toolchain: Xcode, Instruments, and related profiling and testing.

• 
Experience with GPU programming and image processing systems (Metal, OpenCL, CUDA or similar).

• 
Experience with regression testing across many hardware devices, e.g., device labs, device farms, or fleet-based test automation.

Site Manager

Are you an experienced Site Manager who thrives on taking ownership of complex installation projects and leading teams in an international environment? Do you enjoy being hands-on while maintaining a strategic overview of project execution, customer expectations, quality, safety, and timelines? If so, you could be the Site Manager we are looking for.

As Site Manager, you will have overall responsibility for projects from the moment they are handed over by the Project Manager until successful completion on site. Acting as the senior onsite representative, you will lead multidisciplinary teams, coordinate activities across multiple disciplines, and ensure that all installation, commissioning, and testing activities are executed safely, efficiently, and according to plan.

In this role, you will work closely with Project Managers, customers, subcontractors, and internal specialists to secure a successful project delivery. You will be responsible for driving progress, allocating resources, managing budgets and forecasts, and maintaining a high level of quality throughout the installation phase. A key part of the role is building strong customer relationships and ensuring that any project adjustments are properly managed and documented.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Leading and coordinating all onsite activities, including mechanical and electrical installation, commissioning, testing, and final acceptance.

• Managing multidisciplinary site teams consisting of Site Supervisors, Commissioning Engineers, PLC Software Engineers, and WCS/WMS specialists.

• Ensuring compliance with site safety standards, quality requirements, and the company's Site Excellence framework.

• Driving planning, resource allocation, budgeting, forecasting, and schedule management for all site activities.

• Acting as the primary customer contact on site and ensuring clear communication throughout the project lifecycle.

To succeed in this role, you likely hold a degree in Marine Engineering or another relevant technical discipline and have substantial experience managing installation projects on customer sites. You combine strong technical insight with excellent leadership and communication skills and are comfortable taking full ownership of both project performance and team success.

We are looking for a proactive and decisive leader who naturally takes responsibility, remains calm under pressure, and has the ability to navigate competing priorities while maintaining focus on project objectives. Experience within warehouse automation, logistics systems, mechanical and electrical installations, and commissioning activities will be considered a strong advantage.

In return, we offer a key position in a global organization where you will play a critical role in delivering advanced automation and logistics solutions to customers around the world. You will enjoy significant responsibility, a high degree of autonomy, and the opportunity to work alongside skilled colleagues in an international project environment.

Please note that this position requires extensive international travel and long-term assignments at customer sites worldwide.

Scientific Software Engineer for Research Software Engineering Group

The European Spallation Source (ESS) is one of Europe’s largest research infrastructure projects and is building the world’s most powerful neutron source. Through cutting-edge science and technology, ESS will enable discoveries that advance our understanding of materials, energy, health, and the environment.

About the role

The Research Software Engineering (RSE) group develops and maintains critical software systems that make neutron scattering experiments at ESS possible and successful.

As a Scientific Software Engineer, you will contribute to the development of key platforms supporting the scientific user journey, including the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information systems. You will work closely with scientists, software engineers, and stakeholders across ESS to gather requirements, understand user needs, and develop robust software solutions that integrate seamlessly with the wider ESS ecosystem.

The RSE group uses modern web technologies and software engineering practices to deliver high-quality software with a long operational lifetime. In addition, the group is expanding its focus on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning solutions that can enhance the scientific user experience. As part of this effort, you will contribute to new AI-related initiatives and help establish RSE as a centre of expertise and development for AI applications within the Science Directorate.

This position is well suited for an experienced software engineer with a strong technical foundation, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for building software that enables world-class scientific research.

Key responsibilities

• Design, develop, test, and maintain software systems supporting the scientific user journey at ESS.

• Contribute to the development of the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information management systems.

• Gather, analyse, and refine requirements from scientific and technical stakeholders across ESS.

• Design and implement integrations between RSE applications and other ESS services and platforms.

• Apply modern software engineering practices to deliver reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions.

• Contribute to technical and process improvements within the SIMS group.

• Participate in AI and Machine Learning initiatives supporting the Science Directorate.

• Collaborate with scientists, software engineers, and international partners to develop innovative solutions for scientific computing and data management.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing within the team when appropriate.

• Contribute to software architecture discussions and technology decisions within the group.

Required qualifications

• Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Typically 4-7 years of relevant professional experience in software development.

• Experience developing modern web applications and services.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern software development practices.

• Experience gathering requirements and working directly with stakeholders and end users.

• Experience designing and implementing integrations between complex software systems.

• Ability to work independently and manage technical tasks and projects with limited supervision.

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

Desirable qualifications

• Experience working with scientific software, research infrastructures, or data-intensive environments.

• Experience with cloud-based services and distributed systems.

• Experience with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning technologies and their practical application.

• Experience with user-facing platforms, portals, or information management systems.

• Familiarity with modern DevOps practices, CI/CD, automated testing, and container technologies.

• Experience working in international and multidisciplinary environments.

• Experience contributing to open-source software projects.

What we offer

DMSC is located on the DTU campus in Kongens Lyngby, north of Copenhagen, while the ESS neutron facility is based in Lund, Sweden. Together, they form a unique cross-border scientific environment in the Øresund region.

You will join a dynamic and highly collaborative international workplace with colleagues representing nearly 60 nationalities across ESS and DMSC. We offer flexible working conditions, opportunities for professional development, and close interaction between computational science, instrumentation, and large-scale experiments.

Benefits include 25 + 5 annual leave days in addition to public and company holidays, an attractive pension scheme, preventative healthcare benefits, and relocation support for international hires where applicable.

This is a full-time, permanent position based in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, and we need someone who can start as soon as practically possible.
